sources.title: Grouped-Query Attention (GQA) in Modern LLMs
sources.snippet: What is grouped-query attention (GQA), and why do many modern LLMs use it? Grouped-query attention (GQA) keeps the usual set of query heads but uses fewer key and value heads. Several query heads therefore read from the same key-value pair. This reduces the size of the KV cache and the amount of cached data that must be read during autoregressive generation. sources.title: Grouped Query Attention | allbilly/inference | DeepWiki
sources.snippet: Purpose and Scope This document provides technical documentation for the GroupedQueryAttention mechanism implemented in the Qwen3 model. Grouped Query Attention (GQA) is a memory-efficient variant of multi-head attention where multiple query heads share the same key and value heads, reducing the number of key-value pairs that need to be cached during inference.

sources.title: Grouped Query Experts: Mixture-of-Experts on GQA Self-Attention
sources.snippet: Self-attention is central to Transformer performance and is often the most expensive part of the Transformer at long context lengths because its pairwise token interactions scale quadratically with sequence length. Standard dense attention also applies the same set of attention heads to every token regardless of token difficulty or information content.
